doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Being a lucky man whose dreams came true
summary: Berroa reflects on how few immigrant musicians see their dreams fulfilled; Rowe shares his own college dreams.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well you certainly did better than that.

Well yeah. Thanks. I can see that I’m a lucky man. I’m a lucky man because not everybody comes to the United States and fulfills their dreams. Speaking about music you know a lot of musicians from different countries come to the United States with an idea, with a dream and not everybody has been able to see their dreams come true. I’m one of the luckiest ones that I have seen my dreams come true.
When I was in college a certain group of us, we would have dreams about getting a call to play with Buddy Rich or Stan Kenton. You know I dreamt about being a member of Blood, Sweat & Tears.
